correctness.rationale: The conditional one-projection squared-error identity identifies the exact least-information eigenvalue. Positive-price normalization is a bijection, the SDP covering formulation is equivalent, and explicit primal/dual pairs attain d(d+t)/(d+1) below the threshold and d-squared above it. For t<d-squared the dual is strictly positive and the dyadic Frobenius Gram is positive definite, forcing unique equal weights. At/above the threshold a rank-one dual forces all other weights equal and an exact orthogonal eigenvalue condition yields the complete interval and strict-high-price uniqueness. Fraction-based checker verifies 56 exact rational primal/dual cases and all principal minors; it is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2014 unpriced Kaczmarz SDP and the 2015/2016 broader sketch-and-project SDP establish the general information-matrix method, but the inspected original research does not give the cost-normalized regular-simplex classification. New content is the d-squared row-price frontier, its apparently counterintuitive uniform law below threshold, the explicit optimal value for all positive real prices, and uniqueness/complete critical equality cases. Existing simplex reshuffling and planar long-horizon results have different operators/objectives. Inaccessible older specialized material is expressly a residual risk, not silently cleared.
residual_risks: A specialized earlier exact cost-sensitive simplex E-optimal-design solution may be indexed under terminology not retrieved; search coverage is not an independence certificate.

The reported exact optimum is defined for one-step worst-initialization squared-error progress divided by expected projection cost; its optimality does not automatically transfer to long-horizon mean-square decay or realized wall-clock efficiency.

value.rationale: Heterogeneous row-projection costs motivate progress-per-expected-cost rather than generic iteration-count speed. The minimally redundant simplex is canonical and analytically tractable. A quadratic price threshold with uniform sampling persisting unchanged below it, and an exact critical optimizer continuum, gives a nontrivial globally sharp structural answer in every dimension. A direct decision rule obviates numerical SDP solution for this family. It is not claimed to solve arbitrary sampling costs or realized runtime.
